newsitem.title: CANADA: Inco says union recommends new labor deal.
newsitem.headline: Inco says union recommends new labor deal.

text.p: Inco Ltd said on Thursday that union negotiators for the 4,670 striking nickel miners at its Sudbury, Ontario mine would recommend a new contract deal to end a four-week strike.
Inco's Ontario division president Jim Ashcroft said Inco's settlement package was endorsed by union leadership on Thursday afternoon.
He said Inco's final package included improvements to wages, vacation bonuses, pensions and contracting out that striking miners were seeking.

"Our offer is fair and addresses the needs of both young employees and those nearing retirement," he said. "It is also vital to the Division's competitive future and promises that the community of Sudbury will continue to benefit from a strong and competitive nickel industry."
An unidentified spokesman at Local 6500 of the United Steelworkers of America told Reuters that the union expected to hold a ratification vote on the deal on Saturday.
"We should know the results by Saturday night," he said.
Inco's unionized Sudbury workers went on strike at midnight on Monday, June 2, after voting 60.4 percent against a contract offer endorsed by union leaders.
According to Inco's 1997 production plan, the Ontario division was expected to produce about 230 million pounds of nickel, about 200 million pounds of copper and about four million pounds of cobalt.

Inco's Port Colborne, Ontario refinery, which processes cobalt, precious metals and electro-nickel, was not affected by the Sudbury strike. Unionized workers at the refinery approved the contract on Monday, June 2.
